comment: The one pin tying this firmware to the canonical Plasma RGBX v2 module.
This repository does not carry a copy of the Plasma source. CI clones this
revision, builds its rgbx-v2 target against this checkout's packaged SDK, and
requires the result to hash to moduleSha256, which is exactly the module committed
as the RGBX v2 conformance fixture in
fw/tests/extensions/wasm_mvp_runtime/src/plasma_v2_sdk_module.h.
packageSha256 covers the .rgbx container the device would install. It binds the
manifest and a SHA-256 of the exact translation unit, so an edit to the manifest or
to the source text moves it even when the compiled module does not change.
This is a fixture-provenance pin, and it lives inside fw/ so a change to it runs the
firmware gates. The same upstream repository is also pinned for distribution by the
plasma entry in extensions/registry.json, which lives outside fw/ on purpose. The two
are independent: that one selects the .llext a release ships, this one selects the
bytes a firmware test embeds.
Bumping this pin means setting rev to the new upstream revision and moduleSha256 and
packageSha256 to what that revision builds, then regenerating the fixture header.
provisional is required and must be a JSON boolean. Set it to true to name a revision
that is not merged upstream yet: the build then fails unless
RGBX_PLASMA_ALLOW_PROVISIONAL=1, which CI passes on pull requests only. That does not
stop a provisional pin from being merged, because its own pull request is green by
design so the change can be reviewed. What it stops is main staying green with one:
the push-to-main run of sdk-ci gets no allowance and fails until the pin is repointed.
release.yaml never runs sdk-ci, so a release is not protected by a gate it runs
itself; it is protected transitively, by main being green before a release is cut.
